assessment.nobel_worthiness: Turns the cell's ubiquitin-proteasome machinery into a programmable chemical tool: bifunctional degraders and molecular glues make a defined ternary-complex chemistry that removes a target protein rather than inhibiting it. It gave biologists a general tool and explained thalidomide-class drugs mechanistically, with strong biomedical reach.
assessment.attribution: Crews conceived and demonstrated PROTACs; Deshaies contributed the degrader concept and development; Handa identified cereblon as the thalidomide target, which underpins molecular glues. Ciulli, Gray and others made major later contributions, so a three-way split omits real contributors.
assessment.maturity: Reproduced widely across many laboratories and several targets, and degraders are in clinical trials. Recognition is reasonably timely, though clinical validation is still maturing.
uncertainties: Credit is spread over PROTACs and molecular glues, which may need different recognition.
Clinical benefit is not yet fully established; I cannot verify trial outcomes myself.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Nitrogenase is a central enzyme of the nitrogen cycle, and its FeMo-cofactor structure and the mechanism of N2 reduction are a fundamental problem of metalloenzyme chemistry. Structures with the interstitial carbide and mechanistic work on electron and proton delivery show a well-defined chemical reaction under a biological process.
assessment.attribution: Rees solved the original FeMo-protein and cofactor structures; Einsle resolved the interstitial atom at high resolution; Seefeldt defined the mechanistic framework. Dean and Ribbe also made important contributions, so the allocation is uncertain.
assessment.maturity: Decades of independent structural and spectroscopic confirmation, though the full catalytic mechanism and the substrate-binding intermediates are still debated. Recognition is mature, perhaps overdue.
uncertainties: The catalytic mechanism is still unresolved, so the discovery may be seen as incomplete.
Credit among five names is hard to limit to three.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Orthogonal aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase/tRNA pairs let cells incorporate designed chemical groups at defined sites in proteins in living cells. This is a general chemical tool for biologists, used for probes, crosslinkers and therapeutics.
assessment.attribution: Schultz established the approach with Wang, and Chin extended it to eukaryotes, multiple codons and engineered ribosomes. Yokoyama and Mehl contributed structural and practical advances.
assessment.maturity: Broadly reproduced and routinely used across many laboratories for over two decades, so it is mature.
uncertainties: Overlap with other tRNA-synthetase and in vitro translation work could complicate credit.
Wang's and Chin's relative contributions are not easy to weigh.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantitative mass-spectrometry proteomics turned measurement of protein abundance, modification and interaction into a routine analytical chemistry, comparable to the quantitative measurements of metabolite pools that I rely on. It transformed biology and biomedicine.
assessment.attribution: Mann (high-resolution methods, SILAC, deep proteomes), Aebersold (targeted and quantitative proteomics, SRM/SWATH) and Yates (shotgun proteomics) are the strongest trio, while Hunt, Gygi and Heck also made decisive contributions.
assessment.maturity: Very mature, independently validated and used everywhere. It is partly honoured already through the 2002 ionisation prize, which weakens its novelty.
uncertainties: The 2002 Chemistry prize on soft ionisation might be seen as covering the foundations.
The field has many strong contributors, so any trio is contested.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Native chemical ligation makes proteins by chemoselective joining of unprotected peptides, a clean well-defined reaction that gives access to modified proteins, with expressed protein ligation extending it to semisynthesis. It is a mechanistically clear chemical solution to a biological problem.
assessment.attribution: Kent and Dawson developed native chemical ligation, and Muir developed expressed protein ligation and its use on biological problems. Danishefsky and others also contributed.
assessment.maturity: Thoroughly confirmed over thirty years and widely used. Recognition is timely to late.
uncertainties: Whether the prize should recognise the ligation reaction alone or also semisynthesis is open.
Others, including Brik and Liu, made later advances.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Covalent targeting of the KRAS G12C mutant cysteine, together with chemical genetics of kinases, made a protein long thought undruggable accessible to a chemical mechanism and led to approved drugs. It combines clear chemistry with a major biomedical effect.
assessment.attribution: Attribution is simple, since Shokat's group made the decisive discoveries. The one credited name keeps the configuration clean, but a prize might be shared with industry teams that developed the drugs, who are not named.
assessment.maturity: Clinical validation is real, since KRAS G12C inhibitors have been approved, and independent groups have confirmed the chemistry. The field is still evolving, so some caution on timing.
uncertainties: Industry contributions to the approved drugs are not in the credited names.
Durability of clinical responses is not fully known to me.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ionizable lipid nanoparticles are the chemical delivery vehicle that made siRNA and mRNA medicines work, a clear invention with exceptional medical impact in the COVID-19 vaccines. The key chemistry is the pH-dependent ionisable lipid and formulation.
assessment.attribution: Cullis's group developed the early lipid nanoparticle technology with Hope and Madden, while MacLachlan, Anderson and Langer contributed lipid design and delivery advances. Credit is among the most contested on this list.
assessment.maturity: Clinical and commercial validation is overwhelming. Timeliness is reasonable following the 2023 Medicine prize for mRNA modification, although fair attribution is hard.
uncertainties: Dispute over who made the decisive lipid and formulation advances; patent disputes exist.
Possible overlap with the already-recognised mRNA vaccine prize.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantitative measurement of long-range electron transfer through proteins, with the tunnelling-pathway view and the idea of hopping through amino acid radicals, links to radical transfer in enzymes such as ribonucleotide reductase. It is a rigorous chemical account of a biological process.
assessment.attribution: Gray and Winkler were the principal experimentalists, and the credit is clean for two names. Others such as Beratan, Onuchic and Moser/Dutton developed theory and parallel experiments that are not credited in this entry.
assessment.maturity: Decades of independent confirmation, and the interpretation of the pathway and hopping models is stable. Marcus received the 1992 prize for electron transfer theory, which partly lessens novelty.
uncertainties: Overlap with Marcus theory and the omission of Dutton and Beratan.
Less direct medical or tool-like impact than other candidates.
